# Poetry Codex

> Poetry Codex (https://poetrycodex.com) is a free, advertisement-free reading archive of the world's poetry in the public domain. It holds over 187,000 poems and the great epics in their classic translations, from Gilgamesh, Homer and the Mahabharata to the early twentieth century, with the ancient sources of Greece and Rome in prose and verse, and study guides and line-by-line study notes written by its editors. Every text is reproduced in full and is in the public domain; translations were published before 1931 and name their translator. The editors' guides and notes are original.

## What is here

- Poems: https://poetrycodex.com/poem/<poet>/<n>/ (one page per poem, with its source, translator and date)
- Poets: https://poetrycodex.com/poet/<poet>/ (biography and list of works); every poet, earliest first: https://poetrycodex.com/poet/
- Long works and epics, with every book or canto on its own page: https://poetrycodex.com/work/<work>/
- Study guides (summary and analysis of every book, characters, themes, critical debates, key passages, questions and a scholarly bibliography): https://poetrycodex.com/guide/
- Articles by the editors: https://poetrycodex.com/blog/
- Sitemap of all pages: https://poetrycodex.com/sitemap.xml

## Study guides

All guides on one page: https://poetrycodex.com/guide/

## Citing

Each poem page gives its source edition and translator. To cite the editors' study guides: "Poetry Codex editors, '<Title>: Study Guide', Poetry Codex, <URL>, accessed <date>."
